t.E284.agn: It is evaluated on the basis of boron. In 2013 EFSA set a group ADI of 0.16 mg/kg body weight, expressed as boron, for boric acid and borax; this value is based on the no-effect dose in a developmental toxicity study in rats. Adverse effects on the male reproductive system have been reported in animal studies; EFSA stated that regular exceedance of the ADI from the authorised use in caviar alone is unlikely.
t.E284.body: It is absorbed as a boron compound.
t.E284.eff.0.a: Regular exceedance of the daily limit (unlikely from the authorised use in caviar alone)
t.E284.eff.0.t: Adverse effects on the male reproductive system and on development were seen in animal studies; the daily limit is based on these findings
t.E284.eff.0.w: Animal studies; relevant to development during pregnancy
t.E284.eval: In the EU it is authorised only for caviar (sturgeon roe); in the EU classification, boric acid falls under reproductive toxicity (Category 1B).
t.E284.prod: Obtained by treating boron minerals such as borax, kernite or colemanite with sulphuric or hydrochloric acid.
t.E284.pw.0: In the EU, boric acid is classified as toxic for reproduction Category 1B, and EFSA's daily limit is based on a developmental toxicity study; in food it is authorised only in caviar.
t.E284.regx.0: Re-evaluated; group ADI 0.16 mg boron/kg body weight/day.
t.E284.regx.1: Only in sturgeon roe (caviar), at most 4,000 mg/kg expressed as boric acid.
t.E284.regx.2: Reproductive toxicity Category 1B under CLP (H360FD); by Regulation (EC) 790/2009.
t.E284.summary: An acid containing boron. In the EU it is authorised in food only in sturgeon caviar.
t.E284.what: It is a boron compound used as a preservative in sturgeon roe (caviar).
